recipes.name: ps
recipes.summary: run one PowerShell command from bash, no profile

recipes.name: win-which
recipes.summary: every place Windows finds a program on PATH

recipes.name: win-path
recipes.summary: turn a bash path into a Windows path

recipes.name: win-port
recipes.body: netstat -ano | grep LISTENING | grep -E -- ":{1}\s" || echo "nothing listens on {1}"

recipes.name: win-proc
recipes.summary: running processes matching {1}, with pid and memory

recipes.name: win-kill
recipes.summary: stop one process by pid (never by image name)

hints.hint: Git Bash turns /c into a path. Use cmd //c "<command>" from bash
Git Bash turns /PID into a path. Use taskkill //PID <pid> //F from bash

hints.match: is not recognized as (an internal or external command|the name of a cmdlet)
hints.hint: That program is not on this shell's PATH. Bash and PowerShell can have different PATHs; find it with where.exe <name> and call it by full path
Windows PowerShell 5.1 has no && or ||. Use A; if ($?) { B }, or pwsh 7

hints.match: running scripts is disabled on this system
hints.hint: The execution policy blocks .ps1 files. For one run: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <script>
The script has Windows line endings. Convert it: sed -i 's/\r$//' <file>, and add *.sh text eol=lf to .gitattributes
Windows path limit. Run git config --global core.longpaths true, then retry
